sentences.zh: 我过去非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain, is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.

sentences.zh: Whoop还为我提供这些可操作的个性化见解，让我更有意图性，这意味着我在日常生活中能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.zh: 还有人收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、海外纸币，或者八十年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.zh: 山姆探讨了那些构成了我们一部分的回忆、执念和微小宝藏。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the very unprofessional podcast whereby I, your unqualified guide, talk through some of the big changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你的二十多岁心理学》，这是一档非常不专业的播客，由我这个不合格的向导，带大家探讨二十多岁时的一些重大变化

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 与人生转型，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: I hope your week has been well, that something amazing has happened, or you got some, you know, cool news.
sentences.zh: 希望你这周过得不错，发生了什么美妙的事情，或者你听到了一些，你知道的，很酷的消息。

sentences.en: I'm recording this with a little cat on my lap right now, and it's very, very satisfying.
sentences.zh: 我录这期节目时，腿上正趴着一只小猫，感觉真是非常非常惬意。

sentences.en: But this week, we're going to be delving into the chaos, the absolute fucking nightmare of the nine-to-five job.
sentences.zh: 但本周我们要深入探讨的是九点到五点上班的混乱，绝对他妈的噩梦般的日子。

sentences.en: This is a topic that my friends and I talk about all the time, and the general conclusion we most often reach is that the nine-to-five job should be abolished, left for dead.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们经常讨论这个话题，我们得出的普遍共识往往是，朝九晚五的工作制度应该被废除，让它见鬼去吧。

sentences.en: It's not a happy way of life for many, I think, and myself included.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对许多人来说，包括我在内，这不是一种快乐的生活方式。

sentences.en: So today, we're going to talk about how a nine-to-five is not conducive to a healthy, rounded, and happy way of living, especially when we're young.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要谈谈为什么朝九晚五不利于健康、全面和快乐的生活方式，尤其是对我们年轻人而言。

sentences.en: And we're going to have a special guest come on later.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们还会请来一位特邀嘉宾。

sentences.en: But first, let's just talk about some of the psychological concepts behind why a nine-to-five work week is actually just really terrible.
sentences.zh: 但首先，让我们先来聊聊为什么朝九晚五的工作周实际上真的很糟糕背后的心理学概念。

sentences.en: So our work can be a big part of our identity and offer some pretty key insights into what's important to us.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作可以成为我们身份的重要组成部分，并为对我们重要的事物提供一些相当关键的见解。

sentences.en: So it is a really rich area of psychological study.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个非常丰富的心理学研究领域。

sentences.en: And for many people in their 20s, the transition to full-time work is very much like the transition to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 对许多二十多岁的人来说，向全职工作的过渡非常类似于向成年期的过渡。

sentences.en: We have those fun years in university and high school where we have a lot of freedom to work the jobs and the hours we want.
sentences.zh: 我们在大学和高中时期度过了那些快乐的时光，有很大的自由去从事我们想要的工作和工时。

sentences.en: And for many, that means that we have our days and, you know, well, our lives just free to do what we wish with.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这意味着我们的日子，你知道的，我们的生活是自由的，随心所欲地做我们想做的事。

sentences.en: But that can really come crashing down when we enter the workforce and suddenly we have to adapt our lifestyle to the typical nine-to-five work week.
sentences.zh: 但当我们进入职场，突然不得不调整生活方式以适应典型的朝九晚五工作周时，这种状态就会彻底崩溃。

sentences.en: So I've had this experience recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近就有过这种经历。

sentences.en: I work the typical nine-to-five every day, every week.
sentences.zh: 我每天、每周都过着典型的朝九晚五生活。

sentences.en: And after the first few weeks, the novelty kind of wears off and it really started to wear me down and it can be pretty, you know, fucking depressing.
sentences.zh: 在前几周过后，新鲜感消退了，它真的开始把我压垮，而且你知道的，这可能会让人他妈的挺沮丧的。

sentences.en: The thing that really got me was that mononymous procedure of going to the same place every day, the same commute, doing the same silly little tasks surrounded by the same people.
sentences.zh: 真正让我崩溃的是那种单调的程序：每天去同一个地方，同样的通勤，在同样一群人的包围下做着同样无聊的小任务。

sentences.en: And so much of your day becomes devoted to this bigger entity and what's in the interest of this company or organization,
sentences.zh: 你的一天中有很大一部分时间都奉献给了这个庞大的实体，以及这家公司或组织的利益，

sentences.en: which can be, you know, insanely unfulfilling in many instances.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，这可能，你知道的，极度缺乏成就感。

sentences.en: And I especially began to notice this when winter struck.
sentences.zh: 当冬天来临时，我尤其开始注意到这一点。

sentences.en: You wake up at nine, you know, 7.30, the sun's still down, commute to work, maybe blasting some music so you don't feel like, you know, an absolute robot.
sentences.zh: 你九点，不对，七点半醒来，太阳还没出来，通勤去上班，可能还得把音乐开得很大声，好让你觉得自己不像，你知道的，一个彻头彻尾的机器人。

sentences.en: And you finish up after five when the sun is set.
sentences.zh: 而你五点过后下班时，太阳已经落山了。

sentences.en: And where has your day gone?
sentences.zh: 你的一天去哪儿了？

sentences.en: Where is this natural instinct to be active in the sun and outdoors going?
sentences.zh: 这种在阳光下和户外活动的自然本能都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: With the hours you have left, how do you create fulfillment and an identity in so many short hours in such a short period of time when the sun is down and you're exhausted?
sentences.zh: 利用你剩下的时间，当太阳落山而你又精疲力竭时，如何在如此短的时间里创造出成就感和自我认同？

sentences.en: And I've just come to the conclusion it's almost impossible to remain human in the system and to maintain a concept of yourself beyond your function as a worker or as an employee.
sentences.zh: 我得出的结论是，在这个体制中保持作为一个人的状态，并在作为打工人或雇员的功能之外维持自我概念，几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: You know, you just end up having so little time to be yourself and to pursue things that truly do bring you joy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你最终留给自己的时间少之又少，根本没空做自己去追求那些真正能给你带来快乐的事物。

sentences.en: Now, I know this is not the case for anyone.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道这并不适用于所有人。

sentences.en: Some people find work and jobs that inspire them and light a fire under their soul and push them towards really, really great things.
sentences.zh: 有些人找到了能激励他们、点燃内心激情并推动他们走向非常、非常伟大成就的工作。

sentences.en: And some people find it immensely enjoyable and fulfilling to be devoted to people and projects that are bigger than themselves and a sense of purposefulness and productivity.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得，全身心投入到比自己更宏大的事业和项目中，以及那种目标感和成效感，是极其享受和充实的。

sentences.en: There's also that element of money, you know, in a world where we have to pay to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这里还有金钱的因素，你知道的，在这个我们必须花钱才能生存的世界里，

sentences.en: No wonder we've become so conditioned to a system that asks us to sacrifice, you know, the majority of our daily hours to work in an office of something we don't particularly love
sentences.zh: 难怪我们变得如此顺从这样一种体制：它要求我们牺牲，你知道的，大部分日常时间去办公室做一件我们并不是特别热爱的事，

sentences.en: just to afford, you know, the small pleasures in life like rent.
sentences.zh: 仅仅为了负担，你知道的，生活中的一些小确幸，比如房租。

sentences.en: Like I mentioned, this dilemma between being a free spirit and embracing our youth or sacrificing these young years for full-time employment is one I'm sure many of my listeners
sentences.zh: 正如我所提到的，这种在做自由灵魂、拥抱青春与为全职工作牺牲青春年华之间的两难抉择，我相信我的很多听众都曾经历过，

sentences.en: have experienced, especially if you are going through that transition right now.
sentences.zh: 尤其是如果你正经历着那种转型期的话。

sentences.en: It might even be keeping you up at night.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能会让你夜不能寐。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But even if you don't have this experience, I think we can all recognize this intense societal pressure to enter into this system and the corporate world
sentences.zh: 但即使你没有这种经历，我想我们都能认识到这种强烈的社会压力：迫使我们进入这个体制和企业世界，

sentences.en: and work our lives and days away until we're 65, retired, no longer have the bones or the stamina for the life that we actually wanted for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 没日没夜地工作到65岁退休，那时我们已经没有筋骨或体力去过我们真正想要的生活了。

sentences.en: And when I started investigating this and the psychology behind the nine-to-five job in our 20s, it started feeling even more startling
sentences.zh: 当我开始调查这个现象以及二十多岁时朝九晚五工作背后的心理学时，我感到更加惊恐，

sentences.en: and a pretty shitty deal that we've entered voluntarily into.
sentences.zh: 觉得这真是一笔我们自愿签下的糟糕买卖。

sentences.en: And I have had this feeling recently, like at what point did I actually choose this life for myself and come to the conclusion it would bring me happiness?
sentences.zh: 我最近经常有这种感觉，就像我到底是在哪个时间点为自己选择了这样的人生，并断定它会给我带来幸福？

sentences.en: Like how much of that pressure was external or intangible?
sentences.zh: 这种压力有多少是来自外部的或无形的？

sentences.en: Me feeling this idealized equation for a perfect life whereby, you know, you have a good job, that's the foundation and everything else kind of falls around it.
sentences.zh: 我感受到的这种完美生活的理想化公式，也就是，你知道的，你得有一份好工作，那是基础，然后其他一切都会顺理成章。

sentences.en: But enough of my rant.
sentences.zh: 不过我的唠叨就到这里。

sentences.en: Let's just get into the psychology behind full-time work.
sentences.zh: 让我们直接切入全职工作背后的心理学。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about why a nine-to-five job is not ideal for making a living,
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈为什么朝九晚五的工作不是谋生的理想选择，

sentences.en: burnout, exhaustion and the struggle for fulfillment in a modern-day capitalist society.
sentences.zh: 现代资本主义社会中的职业倦怠、精疲力竭以及对成就感的挣扎。

sentences.en: So before we understand the psychological effects of the five-day work week, we have to understand its history.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们了解五天工作周的心理影响之前，我们必须先了解它的历史。

sentences.en: So the truth is this type of work schedule hasn't always been the standard in Australia or many places in the world.
sentences.zh: 事实是，这种工作日程在澳大利亚或世界上许多地方并非一直都是标准。

sentences.en: So basically in the 1900s, factory workers, they were known for being forced to work
sentences.zh: 基本上在20世纪，工厂工人们以被迫工作

sentences.en: 100-hour weeks or more.
sentences.zh: 每周100小时甚至更久而闻名。

sentences.en: But fortunately, after years of activist work and many people fighting, the powers that be change began.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，经过多年的激进主义抗争和许多人的斗争，当权者开始发生改变。

sentences.en: And now the nine-to-five work week has kind of become a standard.
sentences.zh: 现在朝九晚五的工作周在某种程度上已经成为了标准。

sentences.en: And we've certainly been really lucky to have people from the past who fought for these labour rights and for more free time.
sentences.zh: 我们当然非常幸运，有过去的人们为这些劳动权利和更多的空闲时间而战。

sentences.en: However, I think many of us still believe we're not really getting the best deal.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为我们中的许多人仍然认为我们并没有得到最好的待遇。

sentences.en: So there was a study recently, it was a worldwide study, it had over 3,000 individuals all working those classic eight-hour, sometimes more work days.
sentences.zh: 所以最近有一项研究，这是一项全球性研究，调查了3000多名都在进行那种经典八小时、有时甚至更长时间工作的人。

sentences.en: And findings showed that half of these individuals believe they can do their jobs using only five-hour days.
sentences.zh: 调查结果显示，其中一半的人认为他们只需工作五小时就能完成工作。

sentences.en: This means they think they'd be more productive if they worked fewer hours instead of more or a four-day work week instead of five, which really kind of poses the argument
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们认为如果减少工作时间而不是增加工作时间，或者实行每周四天工作制而不是五天，他们的效率会更高，这实际上提出了这样一个论点：

sentences.en: that working eight-hour days and 40-hour weeks aren't necessarily even effective.
sentences.zh: 每天工作八小时、每周工作40小时甚至不一定是高效的。

sentences.en: And further studies have also shown that those who work a nine-to-five job versus those who have flexible work hours, more days off and greater emphasis on ledger,
sentences.zh: 进一步的研究还表明，与那些拥有弹性工作时间、更多休息日且更强调闲暇的人相比，朝九晚五的上班族

sentences.en: they're more likely to express symptoms of depression, anxiety, they're more likely to laugh less, express less satisfaction with how they use their remaining time
sentences.zh: 更有可能表现出抑郁、焦虑的症状，他们笑得更少，对如何利用剩余时间的满意度更低，

sentences.en: and have fewer fulfilling relationships.
sentences.zh: 并且拥有较少令人满足的人际关系。

sentences.en: According to this recent study that I read about, I think it's only around 30% of the US workforce is engaged in their work.
sentences.zh: 根据我读到的这项最新研究，我认为美国劳动力中只有大约30%的人对他们的工作充满热情。

sentences.en: So in other words, they're passionate about their work and they feel strongly committed to their companies.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们对工作充满激情，并对公司有强烈的承诺感。

sentences.en: But that leaves, you know,
sentences.zh: 但这就意味着，你知道的，

sentences.en: 70% of workers who are either not engaged or actively disengaged.
sentences.zh: 有70%的员工要么缺乏工作热情，要么处于积极的消极怠工状态。

sentences.en: So that's 70% of the population who have this work lifestyle, who appear, quite frankly, quite miserable and not really engaged in what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以有70%的人口过着这种工作生活方式，坦率地说，他们看起来相当痛苦，对自己所做的事情并不怎么投入。

sentences.en: And on average, we spend at least 35% of our waking hours at work.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，我们清醒时间的至少35%都花在了工作上。

sentences.en: And if we're not happy in our job, then it tends to have pretty far-reaching impacts on other aspects of our lives.
sentences.zh: 如果我们对工作不满意，那么它往往会对我们生活的其他方面产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: And it affects things, you know, like our relationships, our sleep, physical health, our ability to relax.
sentences.zh: 它会影响诸如我们的关系、睡眠、身体健康以及放松能力等方面。

sentences.en: So what is it about this system that creates such unhappiness from a psychological perspective?
sentences.zh: 那么，从心理学的角度来看，这个系统究竟是什么原因导致了如此多的不快乐？

sentences.en: I think it's important just to break it down from an evolutionary perspective to begin.
sentences.zh: 我认为首先从进化的角度来剖析它是很重要的。

sentences.en: So humans, they didn't evolve to work a nine-to-five job.
sentences.zh: 人类并非为了朝九晚五的工作而进化。

sentences.en: We evolved as hunter-gatherers and our innate instincts, our minds, our bodies, they've evolved to suit this context, not that of an office.
sentences.zh: 我们是作为狩猎采集者进化的，我们的先天本能、大脑、身体，都是为了适应这种环境而进化的，而不是办公室。

sentences.en: Our central nervous system and many of the structures and features of our bodies, including our circadian rhythm,
sentences.zh: 我们的中枢神经系统以及我们身体的许多结构和特征，包括我们的昼夜节律、

sentences.en: fight-or-flight system, sensory systems and cognitive features such as our attention, they've all adapted as a result of that evolutionary environment.
sentences.zh: 战斗或逃跑系统、感觉系统以及诸如注意力等认知特征，都是作为那个进化环境的结果而适应的。

sentences.en: So for example, one of the primary jobs we used to have in a hunter-gatherer society was obviously hunting.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们在狩猎采集社会中的主要工作之一显然是狩猎。

sentences.en: And this involved brief spurts of intense activity followed by large amounts of leisure time.
sentences.zh: 这包括短暂的强力活动爆发，随后是大量的休闲时间。

sentences.en: Similarly, for those who relied primarily on gathering food, this would have required kind of more time invested, but involved large amounts of physical activity,
sentences.zh: 同样，对于主要依靠采集食物的人来说，这需要投入更多的时间，但包含大量的体力活动，

sentences.en: rest time in between, and it was the lifestyle that brought about specific and instantaneous rewards such as finding something edible.
sentences.zh: 中间有休息时间，而且这种生活方式能带来具体且即时的回报，比如找到可食用的东西。

sentences.en: So both elements of this lifestyle have three important aspects that are no longer kind of present in the modern-day work environment.
